stemMd: Why is less energy generally available to organisms at higher trophic levels?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All biomass is transferred intact to the next level.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Energy is created only at the top of a food chain.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Organisms use energy in metabolism and dissipate much of it as heat.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Carbon atoms vanish at each feeding step.

explanationMd: At each transfer, some biomass is uneaten or unassimilated and much assimilated energy fuels metabolism and is lost as heat. Energy transfer is therefore inefficient even though matter can be recycled.

distractorRationale.a: Not all biomass is eaten or assimilated.
distractorRationale.d: Atoms are recycled rather than destroyed.
distractorRationale.b: Energy enters mainly through primary production.
